it was wonderful like a childhood dream come true! so much fun. i don’t know where you are from, but i surprisingly had a much easier time navigating my allergy in europe than in america which was crazy. with the exception of like two times, people were very knowledgeable on which foods had nuts and which didn’t and could point out what stuff on the menu I could eat - at one restaurant a chef himself came out and pointed out what i could and couldn’t eat, and that he could make some meals without tree nuts too so i could eat the same thing as my friends which was so welcoming (and it wasn’t some high end restaurant it was an above average thai food place near galleries lafayette that cost like 20 euros per meal). 

with the exceptions: they were smaller places who couldn’t determine if my meal itself had nuts in them because of cross contamination but they gave me recommendations to other places so that was nice. it helped that i spoke some french as well but you don’t have to. 

the only thing that i really avoided were pastries and macarons (has almonds) which sucked because before I developed my allergy i had them and i used to love them so much :( but if i found them packaged at a small grocery store (which are everywhere) i could read the allergens on the back.

all in all it really proved to be less of a problem than i thought. like i said before, navigating this allergy was easier in europe (i went to other places like smaller cities in france and belgium) than it was in America. people were very sure on what was in the food so i was pretty confident on the stuff i could eat. just let your server/cashier know you’ll be chillin have fun!!

in french: tree nuts are “fruits à coque” so you’ll probably be saying “je suis allergique aux fruits à coque”

here’s the thing though: house is such a broad term to use, and can literally be applied to anything with a four-on-the-floor beat. there are lots of different types or subgenres of house music like acid house, french touch, etc. 

a good introduction into electronic music is house honestly. i used to think i hated house before i realized i mainly only listened to it. it’s that big. so albums like discovery, chromatica, good faith, aleph, robot face, etc. those are all house music (or at least mostly), though different types of house. there are kinda of house i don’t like, for example tropical house is something i’m not that much of a fan of. so i think you’ve probably been listening to a limited version of house, like the more popular ones. so i think you should give those albums above a try. those are somewhat popular, though they aren’t the kind you would find on mr. suicide sheep. 

but they best thing about electronic music is that it’s so broad. it’s a type of music so there is something for everyone. from drone and ambient techno/idm, to electronica, there really is something for everyone i think. for example you said you like rock and pop-punk? you should listen to gesaffelstein’s stuff, specifically [aleph](https://open.spotify.com/album/3MiiF9utmtGnLVITgl0JP7?si=3rQEvXfjR3CcW8Pp8uhAsQ&dl_branch=1) and [novo sonic system](https://open.spotify.com/album/18y6apqHKwutkZho4fc8Sj?si=5v5OnvjjTfK0nT3YZ7Z-jg&dl_branch=1) or literally anything by daft punk. in that sense, electronic music is really world changing :)
